questions.prompt: The crmpyjs pattern catalog lists three boot-time patterns: fail-fast environment parsing, the test-only config fallback, and the shared Prisma singleton. For each, explain its shape, why it works or what it protects, its failure mode, and when you would avoid it.

keyPoints.text: Fail-fast environment parsing reads process env at startup and crashes early on missing or malformed values.
keyPoints.quote: parse process env at startup and crash early.

keyPoints.text: It works because imports cannot proceed with invalid config.
keyPoints.quote: imports cannot proceed with invalid config.

keyPoints.text: Its failure mode: an import-time crash can surprise people who expected lazy config.
keyPoints.quote: import-time crash can surprise people who expected lazy config

keyPoints.text: Avoid it for optional feature flags that should degrade gracefully.
keyPoints.quote: optional feature flags should degrade gracefully

keyPoints.text: The test-only fallback supplies safe defaults only when NODE_ENV is "test", keeping production strict while easing local tests.
keyPoints.quote: keeps production strict while easing local tests.

keyPoints.text: Overusing that fallback turns missing configuration into silent coupling.
keyPoints.quote: overuse turns missing configuration into silent coupling.

keyPoints.text: The shared Prisma singleton reuses one client via globalThis outside production instead of one client per import chain.
keyPoints.quote: reuse one client via `globalThis` in non-production.

keyPoints.text: Its hidden global state can complicate tests, and it is wrong when each tenant or request must isolate DB connections.
keyPoints.quote: each tenant/request must isolate DB connections.

questions.prompt: Walk through the crmpyjs request-handling patterns: thin controller / fat service, route-local Zod validation, the async error forwarding wrapper, and domain error translation. For each, what does it do, why does it work, and what is its failure mode or the point at which it should evolve or be skipped?

keyPoints.text: Thin controller / fat service: the controller reads the request and returns the response while the service owns the rules.
keyPoints.quote: controller reads request and returns response; service owns rules.

keyPoints.text: Its risk is services growing into god classes; for a trivial handler the abstraction is just ceremony.
keyPoints.quote: the handler is trivial and abstraction would be ceremony only.

keyPoints.text: Route-local Zod validation rejects malformed requests before the service runs, and validated data replaces the raw req.body.
keyPoints.quote: validated data replaces raw `req.body`.

keyPoints.text: Its failure mode is duplicated validator helpers across modules, so it should give way to a shared validation middleware once many modules need it.
keyPoints.quote: many modules need a shared validation middleware abstraction.

keyPoints.text: Express does not cleanly handle rejected async route promises, so async handlers are wrapped and errors forwarded with catch(next).
keyPoints.quote: Express does not automatically handle rejected async route promises cleanly.

keyPoints.text: That wrapper's failure mode is forgetting to wrap a new route.
keyPoints.quote: forgetting to wrap new routes.

keyPoints.text: Domain error translation: services throw a domain-aware error that is translated to HTTP once at the edge, so services stay framework-light.
keyPoints.quote: throw domain-aware error, translate once at edge.

keyPoints.text: Throwing a generic Error bypasses the structured codes.
keyPoints.quote: generic `Error` throws bypass structured codes.

questions.prompt: Explain the crmpyjs password hash boundary and the split access/refresh token pattern: what problem each solves, how each is shaped, why the implementation works, when you would not use it, and, for the hash boundary, how plaintext can still leak.

keyPoints.text: The password hash boundary keeps raw password handling out of most code through dedicated hash and verify helpers.
keyPoints.quote: keeps raw password handling out of most code.

keyPoints.text: It works because bcrypt usage is isolated in those helpers.
keyPoints.quote: isolates bcrypt usage.

keyPoints.text: Plaintext can still leak if it is logged before the helper is called.
keyPoints.quote: accidental logging of plaintext before helper call.

keyPoints.text: It is the wrong tool for secrets that are not passwords and need a different algorithm.
keyPoints.quote: secrets are not passwords and need a different algorithm.

keyPoints.text: Split tokens separate short-lived auth from longer-lived session continuity.
keyPoints.quote: separates short-lived auth from longer-lived session continuity.

keyPoints.text: The shape is two token classes with different payloads and storage semantics.
keyPoints.quote: issue two token classes with different payloads and storage semantics.

keyPoints.text: Access tokens stay compact while refresh tokens support server-side revocation.
keyPoints.quote: access tokens stay compact, refresh tokens support server-side revocation.

keyPoints.text: Use it for revocable long-lived sessions; skip it when a simpler stateless token is enough.
keyPoints.quote: a simpler stateless token is enough.
